title: Cobalt Systems - SOC 2 / ISO gap walkthrough & logs retention
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood's SOC 2 / ISO27001 evidence, KMS options, audit log retention, and a controls gap map. Customer needs clarity on HSM vs managed KMS, key rotation SLAs, and data residency for EU PII. Agreed next steps: provide SOC 2 Type II report, controls mapping csv, sample audit log export, and a proposed pilot SOW.
topics: KMS/HSM options and key rotation SLA
next_steps: Jordan to upload SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestation (link) by 2026-05-14
Maya to send KMS architecture diagram and HSM availability matrix by 2026-05-15
Schedule pilot scoping call with infra team (customer) week of 5/18
Share sample audit log export (7 days) via secure link
action_items: Jordan Park: Share SOC 2 Type II and recent ISO artifact (due 2026-05-14)
Maya Chen: Diagram showing KMS vs Bring-Your-Own-Key flow + HSM options (due 2026-05-15)
Priya Narayan: Provide list of retention/legal requirements for EU PII (due 2026-05-18)
Daniel Reed: Confirm procurement timeline and required SOW items (due 2026-05-20)
transcript: Header: Recorded 2026-05-12 16:00 PDT — Duration 47m — Attendees: Jordan Park, Maya Chen, Arjun Patel (Redwood) / Liam Ortiz, Priya Narayan, Sofia Mendes, Daniel Reed (Cobalt)
[00:00] Jordan Park: Hey everyone thanks for joining — we'll run through our SOC 2 and ISO artifacts and then dig into the KMS / logging questions. Does that agenda look okay?
[00:12] Liam Ortiz: Yeah that sounds good. I mainly want to understand what evidence you can provide and how keys are managed for EU data, cause our lawyers are picky about residency and key custody.

[00:28] Maya Chen: Totally — we'll show two typical patterns: Redwood-managed KMS with envelope encryption, and BYOK with customer key material in an HSM. There's trade-offs re: latency and rotation SLAs.
[00:45] Priya Narayan: When you say BYOK, do you mean we host the key in our cloud KMS or an HSM on-prem? We have some on-prem HSMs but prefer KMS with external key import if possible.

[01:03] Arjun Patel: Both supported. We have integrations for AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and bring-your-own-key where the key material can be in an HSM using PKCS#11. There are also options for asymmetric signing only, etc — sorry, a lot of jargon, but we can map to your controls.
[01:27] Sofia Mendes: Quick question — for BYOK, does Redwood ever see plaintext or key material? That's a blocker for us if the vendor can access keys.

[01:37] Maya Chen: Good callout. With BYOK and customer-managed KMS we never have access to key material — only ciphertext and wrapped keys. With our managed KMS we hold wrapped keys but we offer HSM-backed key stores and strict RBAC so access is limited to key ops service accounts. I'll share a diagram.
[02:05] Liam Ortiz: Ok. Also, audit logging — we need logs for every token and admin action for 7 years. Is that feasible?

[02:14] Jordan Park: 7 years is long; we typically retain operational logs for 13 months in the hosted product, but we can support configurable retention for Dedicated/Private and export snapshots for long-term archival. There are cost and storage implications though.
[02:32] Daniel Reed: For procurement they'll want an SOW that guarantees export capability and a sample export format. Do you have a standard log schema?

[02:42] Arjun Patel: Yes, sample audit log exports include timestamp, user, action, request id, model id, resource path, and a hashed token pointer. We'll attach a 7-day example. Caveat: PII redaction lasts, we avoid logging full prompt content unless explicitly enabled and consented.
[03:00] Priya Narayan: Wait — redaction. I need to make sure prompts containing EU PII are either not stored or encrypted. How does that work?

[03:12] Maya Chen: By default we redact sensitive fields in the pipeline and give customers the option to disable content retention for private deploys. For hosted we provide a redact-and-store option plus the ability to turn off storage per-tenant for enterprise accounts.
[03:30] Liam Ortiz: Can you show me the specific control mapping to ISO 27001 A.18 and SOC 2 CC6 like where key rotation and KMS appear?

[03:39] Jordan Park: Yes, we prepared a controls mapping csv that maps Redwood features to ISO annex A and SOC 2 criteria — access control, cryptography, logging, change management etc. I'll drop that in the secure share. It's not perfect, but it's a starting point for your auditor.
[04:02] Sofia Mendes: On the mapping — are those mapped to specific evidence artifacts (e.g., sysadmin checklists, runbooks, screenshots)? Because auditors ask for screenshots and timestamps.

[04:13] Maya Chen: We annotate each control with sample evidence: policy docs, runbook excerpts, configuration screenshots, and the associated report page. We can also generate a time-bound export for an auditor review window if needed.
[04:35] Liam Ortiz: Great. Next — SSO. We use SAML with SCIM to provision and deprovision. How mature is your SCIM implementation?

[04:44] Arjun Patel: SCIM v2 is supported; user provisioning, group sync, and attribute mapping are in our enterprise flow. Deprovision triggers immediate RBAC revocation and we also purge sessions tied to that user upon deprovision.
[04:59] Priya Narayan: Do you log SAML assertions or just the events? We need proof of deprovision times for audits.

[05:08] Maya Chen: We log events including timestamps for SSO logins, SAML assertion IDs (hashed), provisioning events. We avoid storing raw assertions by default for privacy but can capture metadata for auditability.
[05:23] Jordan Park: Quick note — some transcription noise here, sorry — one second —
[05:30] Liam Ortiz: no worries
[05:33] (cross talk) Sofia: — and what's your standard latency hit if we enable envelope encryption with customer KMS?

[05:39] Maya Chen: Usually microseconds to low single-digit milliseconds for each token op; the bigger overhead is on key unwrapping which happens per session or per worker start, not per token. For very high QPS workloads we recommend a caching layer for unwrapped keys.
[06:00] Priya Narayan: And rotation? Our policy requires rotation every 90 days and proof of rotation. Can Redwood automate rotation hooks?

[06:08] Arjun Patel: Yes — rotation is automated for managed keys, and we provide rotation events and artifacts for BYOK flows when keys are rotated on the customer side. We can provide a rotation log for auditors showing key id, rotation timestamp, and thumbprint.
[06:26] Liam Ortiz: If we go Dedicated versus Private, does the trust boundary change? Are you still providing the same attestation material?

[06:35] Jordan Park: The attestation material is the same — SOC 2 and ISO artifacts — but for Private deployments you host the control plane or we provide an on-prem package which gives you more physical control. Evidence collection changes because some artifacts live in your environment.
[06:52] Daniel Reed: Are there any known gaps in your SOC 2 coverage that we'd need to mitigate?

[06:58] Maya Chen: We maintain SOC 2 Type II across our hosted service; there are a few control exceptions around data residency-specific controls which are handled via contractual addenda and configurations for Private/Dedicated customers. The mapping file calls those out in the notes column.
[07:20] Liam Ortiz: We'll need an explicit contract clause about EU data not leaving region for certain datasets. Is that doable?

[07:27] Jordan Park: Yes, region pinning is supported in Dedicated and Private. For hosted we can route to EU regions — but for strict legal obligations we recommend Private or a guaranteed dedicated capacity in EU with contractual commitments.
[07:45] Priya Narayan: On audit logs again: is the log export signed? Our legal team wants tamper-evidence for archived logs.

[07:53] Arjun Patel: We can provide log exports with checksums and PGP signing for archival receipts. For the highest assurance we can provision an object that is ingested into your archival HSM or a write-once bucket you control.
[08:09] Sofia Mendes: Ok, how do you handle deletion requests? If a user requests deletion of all content under GDPR, can we run a scoped job to scrub prompts and embeddings?

[08:20] Maya Chen: Yes, we support subject access and deletion APIs. For hosted customers on enterprise plans we can run account-scoped scrub jobs and provide evidence of deletion. For Dedicated/Private you manage the deletion job but we provide tools and scripts.
[08:35] Liam Ortiz: Let's talk timing. If we need the SOC 2 artifact and a controls mapping by next week for our pre-audit, is that realistic?
[08:43] Jordan Park: Yes — we can provide the SOC 2 Type II report and a prefilled controls mapping by 2026-05-14. The ISO attestation may take a bit longer but we'll include relevant artifacts.
[09:00] (participant asks about network diagrams) Priya Narayan: Please include the network diagram that shows egress controls and subnet isolation for Dedicated clusters.
[09:10] Maya Chen: Will do — I'll include the Dedicated network diagram and the private deployment topology with VPC peering notes.
[09:19] Liam Ortiz: Any constraints with FIPS or specific cryptographic suites?
[09:25] Arjun Patel: We support FIPS endpoints and can run in FIPS mode for certain builds; there are trade-offs with available acceleration libraries, we'll document which ciphers are in FIPS mode.
[09:40] Jordan Park: Quick pause — some background noise on Liam's line, please go ahead if that's me —
[09:47] Liam Ortiz: Sorry — connection is fine now.
[09:51] (silence, then) Daniel Reed: Procurement note — for SOW we'll need a line item for log export and retention beyond 13 months as an add-on. Can you price that?
[10:00] Jordan Park: Yes we'll provide a cost estimate for extended log retention and long-term archival in the next email.
[10:06] Priya Narayan: Regarding RBAC — do you support attribute-based access control (ABAC) or only role-based?

[10:12] Maya Chen: Core is RBAC with groups and policies, but we have a policy engine that allows attribute checks for advanced rules — effectively ABAC-like conditions mapped to groups and resource tags.
[10:28] Liam Ortiz: Cool. Auditor will likely ask for evidence of separation of duties. Do you have an admin review cadence artifact?
[10:36] Arjun Patel: Yes we have quarterly access reviews and a documented process with screenshots from the console showing review runs; we'll include an anonymized example as evidence.
[10:50] (murmur) Sofia Mendes: if we do a pilot, can we get a short SLA for KMS uptime?
[10:57] Maya Chen: For pilot we can offer a service-level target for key ops of 99.9% across the pilot window; Dedicated customers get higher contractual SLAs under reserved capacity agreements.
[11:12] Liam Ortiz: Final item — evidence access. Can auditors access Redwood trust portal or do you create a one-off package?

[11:20] Jordan Park: We provide a Trust Portal with read-only auditor access for some enterprise customers. Alternatively, we can collect a zipped evidence package with time-limited links. We'll propose the approach based on your auditor's preference.
[11:36] Daniel Reed: Great. Let's recap — you will share SOC 2 and mapping, sample logs, KMS diagrams, and cost estimate for retention. We'll confirm legal clauses and procurement timeline.
[11:46] Jordan Park: Correct — I'll send the links and schedule the pilot scoping for next week. Any final questions?
[11:52] Priya Narayan: Nothing else from security side; thanks everyone.
[11:56] Liam Ortiz: Thanks all — talk soon.
End of transcript
